parts.delta: A skip list is an ordered dictionary built from stacked linked lists. The bottom
level holds every element in sorted order; each level above it holds a random s
ubset of the level below, so a search starts at the sparsest level, walks forwar
d until the next node would overshoot, drops one level, and repeats. With a prom
otion probability of one half the expected height is logarithmic in the number o
f elements and so is the expected search, insertion and deletion cost, without a

ny of the rotations a balanced tree needs.

The structure is popular for concurr
ent and persistent stores because an insertion touches only the forward pointers
on the path it descended, which makes lock-free implementations tractable and m
akes the write path easy to reason about under contention. The costs are the one
s randomization always carries: the bounds are expected rather than worst case,
every node pays for its tower of pointers, and the traversal has poor locality c
ompared with a B-tree's wide nodes, which is why on-disk indexes still prefer th
